articles.title: Tata chief flags challenges in India's semiconductor push, calls 'global collaboration a necessity'
articles.summary: India has the potential to become a significant player in the global semiconductor supply chain, but investments must be guided by demand, financial
articles.body: India has the potential to become a significant player in the global semiconductor supply chain, but investments must be guided by demand, financial viability and the ability to execute projects, Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran said on Tuesday.Chandrasekaran said that semiconductors would be fundamental to the country's future and meeting its domestic consumption requirements. He added that India's talent pool, the size of its domestic market and its potential to participate in international supply chains put it in a favourable position."We are in a beautiful spot in India, because we have the talent, we have the domestic market, we can play a part in every global supply chain," he said at the 2026 Bloomberg New Economy Forum.Chandrasekaran also highlighted collaboration with global players as a necessity to build the country's semiconductor ecosystem. Access to technology and the availability of energy would also be important considerations as India develops its manufacturing capabilities."We need partnerships, because we have all the technologies ... But if you design it, definitely we will get there. But you also have to be careful, because you need to keep an eye on energy," he said.Tata Electronics is setting up a fabrication plant in Dholera, Gujarat, with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC) as its partner. The project involves an investment of around Rs 91,000 crore and will manufacture chips for automobiles, mobile devices, consumer electronics, artificial intelligence and other industrial applications. Alongside, the group is developing a semiconductor assembly and test facility in Assam at an investment of around Rs 27,000 crore.The projects are intended to cater to rising domestic demand, reinforce India's semiconductor supply chain and strengthen the country's integration with the global electronics manufacturing ecosystem.'We need to also see where the demand is'Chandrasekaran cautioned that India and businesses should not rush into manufacturing the most advanced chips without first determining whether there was sufficient demand to justify the investment."You cannot be reckless and say that I am going to be putting a 2 nanometre chip (plant). It's just not going to work. So, we need to also see where the demand is," he said.He emphasised that financial viability was a key consideration not only for businesses but also for India and its people. Investments, he said, needed to make commercial sense and support sustainable employment over the long term."And the financially viable thing, you have got to see the sun cross the river," said Chandrasekaran, who was recently given a third five-year term as Tata Sons Chairman amid a boardroom tussle over the group's future.His comments come as the group pursues semiconductor investments while weighing the practical considerations involved in developing the sector. Although the long-term need for semiconductor capabilities is clear, decisions on the scale of investment, the pace of expansion and the technologies to be used remain important considerations.Chandrasekaran acknowledged that businesses operating in the global environment could not expect every aspect of an investment to be predictable. However, he said some fundamental factors remained certain, including energy requirements and the ability to execute projects."But a lot of things are certain. Energy is certain, the game is certain, the ability to execute is certain. And the only thing is how much you ramp up, how fast you ramp up, which technology you go to...," he said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: MDR on UPI transactions over Rs 2,000 deferred; to come into effect post Diwali
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Its official. There will be no MDR on UPI until the festival season is over.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Its official. There will be no MDR on UPI until the festival season is over. The National Payment’s Corporation of India’s The UPI and Services Steering Committee has deferred the implementation of merchant discount rates (MDR) on select person-to-merchant UPI transactions until immediately after Diwali, citing the festive season. The implementation date will be notified separately.The Times of India had reported last week that finance ministry and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) have decided to defer the introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions, seeking to avoid adding to business costs and hitting consumption at a time of economic headwinds, people aware of the matter said. The revised rollout was expected to be pushed to January 2027 from October 15. However,the announcement on Tuesday states that the implementation will be immediately after Diwali.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The MDR framework was approved and notified by NPCI on September 15, with a 0.4% charge for eligible person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. The framework was to take effect from October 15, giving banks, payment aggregators and other ecosystem participants a month to make operational changes.Also read: Pakistan angle under probe? Delhi Police files 4 FIRs over fake posts since Oct 10The decision to defer the rollout comes just days before the scheduled start and follows demands from trade bodies and merchant associations for a January implementation. They have argued that introducing the fee during the festive season, when retail activity and digital payments typically rise, could increase costs for merchants and weigh on sales.The framework was designed to create a revenue stream for the payments ecosystem after more than six years of effectively zero MDR on UPI. The government had said the levy would apply only to specified merchant transactions, with payments up to Rs 2,000 and eligible small merchants continuing to remain free. About 96% of P2M transactions were expected to remain unaffected.The deferment gives merchants and payment companies more time to prepare while allowing the government to avoid introducing a new transaction cost at a potentially sensitive point for consumption.You use AI every day. articles.title: Gold jewellery gets costlier as prices surge 54%; shoppers turn to Rs 10,000-Rs 1 lakh diamond pieces, as jewellers use 18-carat, 14-carat and 9-carat gold to make it more accessible
articles.summary: Gold prices have risen sharply from levels seen in last year’s festive season.
articles.body: Gold prices have risen sharply from levels seen in last year’s festive season. The sharp hike in gold prices is prompting jewellery buyers to consider diamonds as an alternative, with retailers projecting a 15-20% increase in diamond jewellery sales this festive season.Retailers said the Navratri season has begun on a strong footing for studded jewellery, as shoppers look for pieces that offer value while staying within their budgets. The trend points to a broader change in consumer preferences, with diamond purchases increasingly driven by personal choices and everyday use instead of being limited to weddings and other special occasions.Gold prices rise, diamonds are back in focusAs gold jewellery becomes more expensive, shoppers are increasingly exploring diamond-studded ornaments priced between Rs 10,000 and Rs 1 lakh.Also Read | Gold at Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams is pushing middle-class Indian buyers to silver who are getting 650 grams of silver at the same price; some betting silver at Rs 2.3 lakh per kg may hit Rs 4 lakhJewellers are also turning to 18-carat, 14-carat and 9-carat gold for these pieces to keep them within reach of a wider range of buyers. This allows consumers to opt for lighter jewellery without having to compromise on design.Smaller diamonds have become more affordable, making studded jewellery an appealing option for consumers looking to avoid the higher cost of gold ornaments. Prices of small diamonds are around 25% lower than during the 2025 festive season, while gold prices have climbed 54% over the same period."Diamond jewellery sales have witnessed an uptick at Joyalukkas because it fits the budget of consumers as lower caratage gold is used," Joy Alukkas, chairman of pan-India jewellery retail chain Joyalukkas told ET."We are expecting a growth of 20% in diamond jewellery this festive season. However, competition in the retail jewellery space is hotting up as many regional players are expanding their footprint and entering the equity markets with their IPOs."Demand for diamond jewellery meant for everyday use is also picking up. Senco Gold & Diamonds expects sales in this category to rise 20% this festive season. "Earrings, rings, pendants and bracelets in the price range of Rs 30,000-Rs 1 lakh are showing fast movement," said Suvankar Sen, managing director at Senco Gold & Diamonds.Consumers are also changing the way they shop for jewellery, turning to lighter pieces as elevated gold prices push up the cost of traditional ornaments."Even at Rs 25,000, one can get diamond jewellery," Ishu Datwani, founder of Mumbai-based Anmol Jewellers, told the financial daily. "Moreover, the look-to-price ratio of diamond jewellery is much higher. Customers are preferring lightweight gold jewellery now. Earlier, if they bought a necklace weighing 100 grams, they are now settling for 60 grams."The shift is particularly noticeable in the Rs 10,000-Rs 1 lakh segment, where buyers are finding fewer options in gold jewellery. "There is hardly any good gold jewellery in the Rs 10,000-Rs 1 lakh price bracket," said Colin Shah, managing director of Kama Jewelry. "So, consumers are preferring diamond jewellery. Smaller stones have become popular in this price range."Also Read | Unscrupulous jewellers may use fake stamps to mark your gold: As hallmarking charges rise to Rs 75 from Rs 45 Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council flags risk of rise in fraudstersDemand is also growing for modern diamond jewellery designs that can be worn regularly, rather than being reserved for weddings or other special occasions."With gold prices at elevated levels, we expect diamond jewellery to see increased interest this festive season," said Supriya Kataria, founder of Kumari Fine Jewellery. "Consumers are increasingly looking for pieces that offer distinctive design, versatility and the flexibility to be styled beyond a single occasion." Kataria expects demand for diamond jewellery to increase by 15-20% this festive season.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘I’m strapped every month.’ Seniors struggle as inflation continues to outpace Social Security benefits
articles.summary: Many senior citizens are finding that their Social Security benefits are not keeping pace with the rising cost of living. The payments are adjusted every year based on inflation, but the annual cost of living adjustment doesn’t match the actual increase in expenses.
articles.body: When Stephanie Zebrowski retired and started collecting Social Security in 2018, she was able to get by on her monthly payment with a little left over before the next one arrived. That’s no longer the case. Zebrowski, who worked as a financial editor at a brokerage firm, now finds that the $2,200 monthly payment she receives (after her Medicare premiums are deducted) has not kept up with inflation in recent years. That’s forced the 75-year-old to drain her savings to pay for essentials – such as groceries, gas, doctors’ visits and utilities – and make some unpleasant decisions. Zebrowski, who once considered herself middle class, started visiting a food bank last year and keeps her home colder than she’d like in the winter, even though it aggravates her arthritis and leaves her in pain. She’s had to start creating meals “out of practically nothing,” adding that she’s “learning to like beans.” “I’m strapped every month,” said Zebrowski, who lives in rural Jefferson, New York. “I’m spending almost every penny. It didn’t used to be that way.” Like Zebrowski, many senior citizens are finding that their Social Security benefits are not keeping pace with the rising cost of living, especially in recent years. The payments are adjusted every year based on inflation, but many older Americans and their advocates have long said that the annual cost of living adjustment (COLA) formula doesn’t match the actual increase in expenses. This year, the bump was 2.8%, or an additional $56 per month for the average retiree, who receives $2,071 a month. But a $17.90 increase in the standard monthly Medicare premium – the second-largest hike, in dollar terms, in the program’s history – to $202.90 ate into that raise. The 2027 monthly adjustment, which is scheduled to be announced on October 14, could be around 3.5%, based on early indications. That would provide a retiree with around $72 more a month. But the benefit boost won’t go that far when the price of gas, beef, healthcare and other needs have soared, Mary Johnson, an independent Social Security policy analyst, told CNN. “The inflation we have had in recent years has not gone away. It has not disappeared completely,” she said. “It just heated right back up again with the war in Iran.” (Medicare’s standard premium is forecast to increase $6.60 a month for 2027, according to the program’s trustees.) Less buying power Social Security benefits have lost 13.7% of their buying power over the past decade, according to a recent analysis by The Senior Citizens League, an advocacy group. Put another way, a dollar of benefits in 2016 is only worth 86 cents today. That’s taking into account increases of 5.9% in 2022 and 8.7% in 2023 when inflation skyrocketed after the pandemic. Payments would have to jump by nearly $296 a month, or about $3,550 annually, to restore their buying power for the average beneficiary, the analysis found. Many older Americans depend on Social Security for a large portion of their income and can’t easily adjust to higher prices, Shannon Benton, the league’s executive director, told CNN. “Gas prices are going to be gas prices, right? You can’t substitute that. You can’t substitute your medications for something else,” Benton said. “These are things that there’s just no wiggle room for seniors.” Lawmakers, advocates and think tanks have floated myriad ideas for changing Social Security’s annual adjustment, though they haven’t gone far on Capitol Hill. One proposal would shift the formula to an inflation index tied to price changes based on the spending patterns of senior citizens, known as CPI-E. However, other measures would curtail the COLA as part of an effort to improve Social Security’s overall finances. Selling possessions Pat and her husband, who asked that their last name not be used for privacy purposes, are both around 75. She said they had been able to make ends meet on Social Security and savings because her husband did some handyman jobs for their neighbors in their Florida senior community. But health issues forced him to stop this summer, leaving them dependent on credit cards to pay for groceries, gas, medical and dental care, medicine and other expenses. They used to pay off the balance each month but can no longer do so. Big increases in home and auto insurance premiums over the past two years have added to their financial strain. Though Pat said a 3.5% adjustment would be better than they’ve received in some prior years, it’s still insufficient to keep up with all the other cost increases. “These little raises just aren’t enough,” said Pat. “We’re still trying to catch up from previous years.” The couple, who receive a total of roughly $2,850 a month after Medicare premiums are deducted, estimate they are about $1,000 short each month, even though they cook at home nearly every night and don’t take vacations. A looming concern is the expiration of the interest-free period on their credit card early next year. The next step is to sell some of their possessions, like her husband’s tools. “There’s nowhere else to cut,” Pat said. For Peter Jovanovic, Social Security’s annual increases never fully kept up with inflation. But the 69-year-old said his roughly $1,700 monthly check buys considerably less these days since “everything has gone up in price.” A former truck and taxi driver who had to stop working in his early 50s for medical reasons, Jovanovic had been able to get by because he found a cheap apartment to rent in upstate New York. However, he was then hit with a big rent increase after being forced to move because of issues with his landlord. That left him thousands of dollars in credit card debt that he’s been unable to whittle down. Though he’s now living in subsidized senior housing, Jovanovic is still feeling the bite of higher grocery prices and utility costs. He doesn’t own a car, and his friends have started asking him to chip in for gas when they drive him to the supermarket and on other errands. Taxi and Uber rides cost more, too. The estimated 3.5% adjustment for 2027 wouldn’t do him much for him since “everything is so expensive,” he said. He thinks he’d get about $57 more a month. “It doesn’t come close to what I need to live halfway comfortable, just to afford little things in life,” he said. “I don’t have any luxury stuff.”

articles.title: RBI taking steps to support rupee, says FM Sitharaman; what the central bank is doing
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday addressed rupee's depreciation over the recent months saying that the fall has been significant
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday addressed rupee's depreciation over the recent months saying that the fall has been significant and much of it is driven by global challenges. The FM added that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is taking steps to stabilise rupee and curb volatility.Back in May, the currency tumbled to its record low of 96.96 per dollar but rebounded in recent weeks.Earlier in the session, rupee strengthened by 82 paise to 94.96 per dollar on the interbank order matching system on Tuesday, gaining nearly 0.7% from its previous close.The gains come after RBI introduced a series of measures aimed at curbing dollar demand.These include restrictions on cancelling and rebooking foreign exchange derivative contracts, tighter documentation requirements for currency transactions, a 20% foreign exchange risk reserve for specified transactions and a special dollar window for public sector oil marketing companies.Here’s what the apex bank is doing: 1. Restricted cancellation and rebooking of forex contractsThe RBI has restricted the cancellation and rebooking of foreign exchange derivative contracts involving rupee. The move is expected to reduce market activity by preventing repeated cancellations and rebookings that can add to transaction volumes."With the new measures, RBI has made it more expensive for importers to hedge. Also, the volume in the market should see a decline given cancellation and rebooking of contracts are not going to take place," the ICICI Bank report said.2. Cut the limit for transactions without documentationThe central bank has reduced the threshold for foreign exchange derivative transactions that can be undertaken without establishing the underlying exposure to $5 million from $100 million.The move aims to tighten oversight of currency transactions and curb dollar demand driven by expectations of further rupee depreciation rather than genuine business requirements.3. Tightened documentation to prevent multiple hedgesThe RBI has introduced additional documentation requirements to ensure that the same exposure is not hedged multiple times.The measure comes as importers continue to seek protection against rupee depreciation, while exporters have remained on the sidelines rather than selling dollars. According to ICICI Bank, this imbalance has added to demand for the US currency, while forward premia have increased over recent months.4. Introduced a 20% foreign exchange risk reserveThe RBI has introduced a foreign exchange risk reserve requirement of 20% for specified import-related current account derivative transactions exceeding $2 million.The measure is expected to affect liquidity conditions alongside the central bank's decision to increase the daily cash reserve balance requirement from 90% to 99% of the prescribed cash reserve ratio requirement.According to the ICICI Bank report, the two measures would sterilise around 0.4-0.6% of net demand and time liabilities (NDTL). The report also said the measures had pushed bond yields higher.5. Opened a special dollar window for oil marketing companiesThe RBI has provided a special window for public sector oil marketing companies to meet their dollar requirements. The arrangement takes their dollar demand out of the regular foreign exchange market in the immediate term.However, ICICI Bank cautioned that sustained currency stability would depend on broader external conditions, particularly capital flows and crude oil prices.How could RBI's measures affect rupee?The measures seek to address the imbalance between importers' demand for dollar hedging and exporters' willingness to sell dollars. Higher hedging costs and restrictions on contract rebooking are expected to bring hedging activity closer to equilibrium and ease demand for the US currency."All of these measures put together should ensure that the hedging ratio should move towards an equilibrium and thus cool off the demand for Dollars and thus the depreciation pressure on the currency," ICICI Bank said in its latest report.However, the longer-term direction of the rupee will depend on capital flows and crude oil prices, according to ICICI Bank. While the special dollar window could ease immediate demand in the regular foreign exchange market, sustained stability will depend on these broader external factors.You use AI every day. articles.title: Why Meta is betting its future on computers you wear on your face
articles.summary: It wasn’t your typical concert experience.
articles.body: It wasn’t your typical concert experience. I watched Billie Eilish from a perspective that felt like I wasn’t in the audience or behind the scenes, but somewhere in between: hovering near the stage alongside the singer as she grasped a fan’s hand in the front row. This is what it’s like to watch a clip from Eilish’s 3D tour special shot in Arizona and Manchester, England, with Meta’s new VR Glasses. CNN tried the glasses at Meta’s offices in New York last week ahead of their launch in the spring. Meta is banking on experiences like Eilish’s show to make its new eyewear a hit. Those glasses, along with camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses launching Tuesday, are part of the social media giant’s decade-long ambition to develop what it believes will be the next version of the personal computer. Meta’s previous efforts in this space and its big bet on the metaverse have largely flopped, but the company is convinced things will be different this time. It’s betting that integration with AI agents, stylish designs and more advanced display technology will convince consumers the glasses are the future, despite widespread privacy concerns that have prompted bans and global pushback. Using Meta’s new glasses Meta is pitching next year’s new VR glasses as a computer, game console and movie theater in one. The glasses, which are priced at about $1,300, aren’t anything like the Quest VR headsets Meta has been selling for years, which weigh about 18 ounces and look like a visor or helmet rather than glasses. Instead, the new version resembles a giant pair of sunglasses and weigh about 3.5 ounces. That’s because the computing components are stored in a separate module attached to the glasses with a wire. Users interact with apps by using their eyesight as a mouse and tapping their thumb to their index finger to click. These gestures were easy to learn, although scrolling took a little practice. That involved making a fist and moving my thumb along my index finger as if it were a trackpad. The VR glasses seem to function as a substitute for personal computers and televisions. A user can watch a movie or work across multiple displays like they normally would with their laptop or flat screen. The goal, said Ryan Cairns, Meta’s vice president of VR, is not to replace existing computers but to expand how and where consumers can use them. “I can put VR glasses on in the plane and basically have like three monitors’ worth of work in front of me,” he said. Meta’s Ray-Ban AI glasses, on the other hand, are meant to be worn all day like normal glasses but can handle some of a smartphone’s tasks like getting directions, listening to music and answering questions. Its newest Ray-Ban glasses don’t have a camera, excluding a controversial feature that raised widespread privacy concerns. The glasses have speakers and microphones, but Meta says the mic is limited to phone calls and talking to its AI assistant. It’s like having AirPods built into your glasses. The idea isn’t new. Amazon has been selling Alexa-enabled smart glasses with microphones and speakers since 2019, and a wave of startups have also launched audio glasses without cameras. Meta decided two years ago that it wanted to launch audio-only AI glasses in 2026 because people frequently use their glasses for talking on the phone or listening to podcasts, said Alex Himel, Meta’s vice president of wearables. Meta also still sells other glasses with cameras and launched an upgraded version of those spectacles last month called the Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3. The new glasses have a lighter design, a shortcut button and longer battery life, according to the company. Meta’s quest to own the future of computing Meta missed out on the mobile boom, ceding control of the tech devices that serve as the portal to its services to companies like Apple, Google and Samsung, thus interfering with Meta’s core advertising business. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said in 2022 that an iPhone optional setting that blocks apps from tracking users across the internet would cost the social media behemoth $10 billion in earnings that year. Meta has spent more than a decade trying to reduce its dependence on hardware makers by releasing everything from a Facebook-branded phone to a smart home hub and VR headsets. “There was always a very strong desire: ‘How do we have people on our own platform so we have a little bit more control?’” said Ash Saulsbury, CEO of AI company Awear, who worked in Meta’s wearables division from 2017 to 2019. Smart glasses are gaining popularity, with shipments expected to grow 263% in the first half of 2026 and more than 7 million AI glasses sold by Ray-Ban parent EssilorLuxottica last year. But those glasses have sparked privacy concerns, and Meta’s previous hardware efforts failed to excite consumers. The company’s Reality Labs division, which includes its smart glasses and VR headsets, continues to lose money while VR headset sales have been declining industry-wide. “The glasses are still a little bit of a solution chasing a problem,” said Daniel Newman, CEO of technology market research and advisory firm Futurum. For Meta, there’s more at stake than just a market share of the tech products needed to operate apps. Meta’s new hardware could give consumers more direct access to its Muse AI agent, which is key in determining how it compares with rivals like OpenAI and Google in the AI race. With glasses like the Meta Ray-Bans, users simply speak to the assistant and show it what’s in their surroundings rather than opening an app and typing a question or taking a photo. For the VR glasses, Muse will be able to work across multiple projects and tasks managed across various virtual windows and apps, said Cairns. The glasses will ship with Muse, including support for the new Muse Wonder model announced on Monday and any other updates between now and then, he added. Still, Meta is taking a chance that consumers are willing to add another device to their lives, especially as AI agents become more prominent in gadgets people already own. The optimistic view hinges on how much AI mirrors the smartphone boom, according to Jitesh Ubrani, who covers consumer tech for market research firm The International Data Corporation. He compared Meta’s AI and glasses gamble to the rise of Uber or Lyft, as hailing a car ride through an app only became common with the growth of smartphones. “Consumers essentially are just seeing AI today as a simple chatbot,” he said. “They don’t realize how powerful and capable it can be. And both AI and these glasses kind of go hand in hand right now.”

articles.title: Why JPMorgan CEO Jamie is concerned about large global fiscal deficits
articles.summary: The bottom line on debt.
articles.body:
JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) CEO Jamie Dimon still sees ballooning US deficits as a major hazard.

It's one of the key risks called out in the bank's earnings release on Tuesday, alongside "sticky inflation" and "elevated asset prices."

Dimon told Yahoo Finance on a media call that he "wouldn't use the word most concerned" when describing his views on large deficits relative to the other economic risks he mentioned.

However, Dimon continued, "I think it's a global issue about these global deficits. They haven't been going down, and you know, it includes China and includes Europe and includes other countries and stuff like that. And I don't know when and how that might bite. I just think it creates another source of, you know, potential risk. So then change, you know, it also changes the supply and demand of capital, which you see both there and [with] AI."

JPMorgan reported mixed second quarter earnings. The bottom line fell short of estimates, but it gave a more upbeat outlook for 2027 than some expected.

articles.title: Netflix could stop its stock free-fall with these 4 actions: KeyBanc analyst
articles.summary: Changes need to come to Netflix.
articles.body:
Netflix ( NFLX ) won't be spending the rest of 2026 integrating its once-sought-after prize in Warner Bros. Discovery. That pure joy goes to the well-paid exec team cobbled together by Skydance ( SKYD ) media titan David Ellison.

But what the streaming pioneer should do, Wall Street says, is articulate a plan on its Oct. 20 earnings call to arrest the stock's crash. Shares are down 25% this year and have steadily declined since mid-April.

The stock has been crushed primarily on concerns about waning viewership. Pressures on Netflix have mounted from Google's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) YouTube and more sports finding their way to Amazon ( AMZN ) Prime. Netflix's recent original content has also been ho-hum, at best.

KeyBanc analyst Justin Patterson said in a note on Tuesday that he would like to hear four actions from Netflix management next week.

We don't think Patterson is alone in hoping for clarity on these fronts:

"The first action is content investment. We are already seeing this in areas like live events (which represents ~5% of content spend, and will continue to be measured) and licensed (which underperformed in 2H25 and has had improved content coming in over the course of 2026). As the content quality improves, we believe this could support both pricing power and ads monetization."

"The second action is product. Again, this has been occurring over the past year through areas like the new home screen and AI recommendation models. The new home screen is particularly interesting as it promoted live events and gaming more at the start, which we believe had some negative impact on engagement (i.e., recommendation algorithms were less optimized here than for series and films). As Netflix has learned more about how to promote this content, we believe this headwind is fading. We also believe there is more potential for TF1 type deals. Over a longer time horizon, we believe both gaming and potentially another ad tier could become more meaningful levers."

"The third action is operating expense reductions. Puck recently wrote an article about Netflix planning a roughly 5% workforce reduction, which would correspond to 800-850 employees. From 2019-2025, Netflix's headcount has increased from ~8,600 to ~16,000. Given the size of the company today and potential savings from AI, we suspect there is room for some degree of expense realignment."

"Finally, we believe it could make sense to explore a dividend. Most media and entertainment stocks have paid dividends, and we have observed more large-cap internet companies doing the same to broaden the shareholder base (e.g., Alphabet, Meta ( META ). While this would not change the growth discussion, we do believe it could improve investor sentiment, support the P/E multiple, and potentially lessen the focus on large M&A."

articles.title: French fridge fright: Why supermarkets have become target for hackers
articles.summary: More than 500 shops across France were hit in a major cyberattack on freezers, which caused tonnes of food to perish.
articles.body:
Hundreds of French supermarkets have suffered unprecedented cyberattacks resulting in tonnes of food perishing and raising fears about the vulnerabilities of food systems to advanced technology.

The attacks, which appeared to target internet-linked refrigeration systems manufactured by a Danish company, raised the temperature of fridges and freezers to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122F) at more than 500 shops and supermarkets across the country. Supermarkets confirmed the attacks on Monday.

France’s cybersecurity agency has advised companies operating affected freezer models to immediately disconnect them from the internet – or restrict access to them – and to perform software updates.

It is unclear who may have been behind the attacks, but authorities say they have now launched an investigation.

Hackers gained internet access to the refrigeration systems and remotely cranked up temperatures in freezers and fridges to 50C during the night when shops were closed. Millions of euros worth of food was spoiled, according to retailers. In some cases, the raised temperatures sparked fires or melted equipment.

French supermarket groups E-Leclerc, Intermarche, Carrefour, Monoprix and Cooperative U were all hit.

At least 300 of Intermarche’s stores and its Netto brand were affected. Cooperative U said more than 100 of its supermarkets were targeted, while Carrefour said 80 supermarkets were affected and Monoprix reported that about 5 percent of its roughly 490 stores were hit.

Officials are still investigating who launched the attack and how it was carried out. French TV channel BFM reported that the attackers appeared to have remotely triggered a forced defrosting option in the refrigeration systems.

The systems targeted are built by Danish manufacturer Danfoss, according to France’s government cybersecurity agency. The refrigeration models attacked included the AK-SM800 and AK-SC355.

Danfoss told the AFP news agency that most of the affected control systems were “legacy” products that had “outdated firmware”. The company said it had previously advised supermarkets to update them.

AFP also reported that officials are liaising with other European countries which may have been affected.

It is unclear exactly how much food has been lost. The attacks come after President Emmanuel Macron ordered last month that the country’s critical infrastructure be protected from Russian “hybrid attacks”.

Have supermarkets been hit by cyberattacks before?

Yes. Attacks like these have been reported in other parts of Europe and in the United States.

In April 2025, British retailer and supermarket chain Marks and Spencer suffered a sophisticated ransomware attack that the company said cost it approximately 300 million pounds ($397m) after it was forced to suspend online and app orders. The attack was orchestrated by a hacker group called Scattered Spider, using ransomware from DragonForce, another criminal group. Ransomware attacks involve using malicious software to hide essential data unless a ransom is paid.

According to UK media, the same hackers also tried to attack Co-op and the iconic Knightsbridge store, Harrods.

Similar reports have also emerged from the US. In June 2025, United Natural Foods, a frozen food company which supplies big supermarket brands such as Whole Foods, said it had discovered a cyberattack that forced it to take its systems offline. The company did not reveal the nature of the attack.

In November last year, Ahold Delhaize USA said it was the victim of a cyberattack that disrupted operations at more than 2,000 stores, including Hannaford, Food Lion and Stop and Shop.

They are an easy target and the consequences can be widespread.

As food and agricultural systems increasingly digitise, analysts say supermarkets selling perishable foods are increasingly vulnerable to attacks due to the nature of their stocks.

The rising sophistication of cyberattacks now means that common people and local, third-party companies relying on big chains for business are also falling victim as attacks disrupt supply chains, experts say.

Speaking to Al Jazeera, tech and cybersecurity analyst Steven Lachance said smart appliances connected to the internet will always be vulnerable as hackers seize on security lapses to log in to the systems remotely and trigger malicious features.

“It’s the new reality of having these connected equipment,” Lachance said, pointing out that attacks could evolve to target medical or energy systems.

“This should come as a global wake-up call … Throughout society, we have connected infrastructure that is live on the internet, and that can be hacked. It’s a new reality, and we absolutely need national and international measures to prevent those attacks; otherwise, it’s just going to keep happening,” he warned.

articles.title: Getty Images is going private after failed Shutterstock merger
articles.summary: Getty Images intends to file for bankruptcy and go private as part of a $533 million restructuring agreement with Koch Equity Development.
articles.body: Getty Images intends to file for bankruptcy and go private as part of a restructuring agreement after its plans to merge with rival stock platform Shutterstock fell through earlier this year. On Monday, Getty announced it had secured $533 million from the Getty family and Charles Koch’s investment firm to cut its debt and take the company private, outlining plans to undergo a prepackaged Chapter 11 process “in the coming weeks.” The restructuring effort is expected to be wrapped up by the end of this year, with no anticipated impact on content contributors, partners, customers, or employees globally. Once completed, the company will be entirely owned by Getty family affiliates ⁠and Koch Equity Development. The agreement serves to rescue the financially struggling platform, which had more than $1.3 billion of debt as of June 30th according to regulatory filings. Bloomberg reported in September that Getty had entered a 30-day grace period for operations after failing to make interest payments on its unsecured notes. This follows Getty walking away from a $3.7 billion transaction with Shutterstock in July in response to restrictions imposed on the merger by a UK regulator. This upended a decision granted by the US Department of Justice in February, which gave the agreement “unconditional antitrust clearance.” Both Getty and Shutterstock face ongoing pressure from generative AI services that enable users to quickly generate custom images instead of locating stock and paying licensing fees. Getty has its own AI generator, but competition is fierce and the company hasn’t clearly laid out how it’ll “support its future growth.” “Getty Images is uniquely trusted around the world as the unparalleled leader in premium visual content,” said Getty co-founder Mark Getty. “This transformational transaction is underpinned by the strength of the business and the significant growth potential we see ahead.”

articles.title: Apple debuts HomeView hub as it reinvents smart home strategy
articles.summary: Apple debuted its HomeView smart home device.
articles.body:
Apple ( AAPL ) is reinventing its smart home strategy with its new HomeView hub, the HomePod Mini 2, and Apple TV 4K .

Sporting a seven-inch Liquid Retina Display, the HomeView is designed to sit on a counter in its built-in speaker mount or be mounted to a wall. The $299 HomeView is designed to serve as the home base for your smart home and goes on sale Nov. 13.

According to Apple, HomeView can recognize up to six household users via facial recognition and serve up their specific apps, notifications, and more. It can also play music and podcasts, make FaceTime calls, or look up quick video recipes in the kitchen.

Users can control smart home devices ranging from lights and locks to thermostats and more, check their calendars, and interact with Siri AI to do things like find their keys via AirTags.

Apple has dipped its toes into the smart home space over the years, including with the original HomePod, HomePod mini, and Apple TV, as well as software like its Home app, but has never offered a full-fledged hub like the HomeView before.

Apple ceded much of the smart home space to rivals Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) and Amazon ( AMZN ), which sell their Google Home and Amazon Alexa hardware lines. But the HomeView could change that.

There are a number of do-it-yourself smart home options that allow users to set up a control center for their devices by mounting iPads on them. But the HomeView should provide a far easier, more cohesive offering for everyday consumers.

Apple is also launching a new line of accessories built in collaboration with LG Electronics ( 066570.KS ) and Schneider. Called Apple Home Collection, the devices include a new LG in-home camera that can monitor your home and then turn the camera to face down when you enter the house for privacy.

An outdoor camera can monitor deliveries and remember familiar faces. An LG door camera and lock can recognize your iPhone as you approach and quickly let you inside.

Setting up the devices is as straightforward as connecting a pair of AirPods. Apple is marketing the Home Collection to individuals seeking products that easily integrate with the company's ecosystem and offer robust privacy features.

The HomeView will be a major test for newly minted CEO John Ternus, who took over the top spot from Tim Cook on Sept. 1 and is reportedly angling to focus more on hardware and design.

In addition to the HomeView, Apple also unveiled the $149 HomePod mini 2. Complete with new colors and Siri AI integration, the HomePod mini 2 allows you to do things like add events to your family calendar and ask about broad world knowledge.

articles.title: Wall Street, crypto firms could face scrutiny if Democrats win majorities in midterms
articles.summary: A Democratic victory in Congress would give Democrats powerful tools to probe industries that have benefitted from Trump administration’s policies.
articles.body: A Democratic victory in one or both chambers of Congress would not stop President Donald Trump’s administration from handing regulatory ​breaks to Wall Street banks, prediction markets and crypto firms, but it would give Democrats powerful tools to probe the industries and their watchdogs. Polls suggest Democrats are poised to win the House ‌of Representatives and have an edge in the race for the Senate. If the party prevails in either chamber, it would gain subpoena power, larger investigative staffs and the power to call in agency heads and corporate CEOs to testify, creating headaches and potential legal entanglements for those under scrutiny. “Everything that has gone on in the first two years of this administration is fair game for investigations,” said Kevin Edgar, a partner at BakerHostetler and former chief counsel of the House Financial Services Committee. The administration’s financial policy agenda includes easing rules and supervision it ​says are too onerous and impeding economic growth, while promoting innovation that it says will boost the economy, including crypto and prediction markets. Democrats are already preparing to investigate Trump’s and his family’s ties to the crypto ​and prediction market industries, Reuters reported. They say such dealings are a conflict of interest. The party has also been pushing for more oversight of prediction markets, which they say ⁠may be creating new avenues for misconduct and undermining national security by allowing government insiders to broadcast confidential information. Prediction markets say they vigilantly guard against misconduct. Asked about such potential probes in a September 30 phone interview, Representative Ro Khanna, ​a Democratic member of the House Oversight Committee, told Reuters: “I absolutely think we need to look at these financial transactions, these crypto transactions, and see if any of our national security has been compromised.” Crypto industry worries Crypto ​executives said they are especially worried that Rep. Sean Casten may challenge Maxine Waters, currently the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, for the chair if Democrats win. Punchbowl News reported last month that Casten had weighed such a move. His spokesperson declined to comment. Casten has been a vocal proponent of probing the administration’s crypto ties and of tougher crypto rules. In 2024, he introduced a bill curbing crypto tools he said aid money laundering. He also voted against the industry’s Clarity Act bill in 2025, saying it would ​put Americans at risk. “He is no friend of the industry,” said Ron Hammond, head of policy and advocacy at Wintermute, a crypto trading firm. The White House did not respond to a request for comment. A spokesperson told Reuters last ​month that Democrats plan “to obstruct and baselessly target President Trump’s commonsense agenda.” The administration says supporting crypto and prediction market innovation will keep American jobs and capital onshore. AI and bank CEOs likely targets Other likely Democratic targets include Trump’s regulators, which have relaxed oversight of ‌lenders and ⁠pulled back on enforcement. Wall Street’s role in financing the AI boom and data centers, a contentious election issue, as well as its influence on housing and other affordability challenges, is also likely to draw scrutiny, said attorneys and analysts. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee and a veteran Wall Street critic, is seen as the frontrunner to chair that committee. She has recently focused her criticism on major AI companies, saying the industry has gained special access to the administration and influence over policy. Both Warren and Waters have also repeatedly raised concerns over affordability, including housing issues, and accused the administration of eroding consumer finance protections. When Waters previously ran the House committee, she called the CEOs of ​the largest US banks to testify on a range of ​issues, and is widely expected to do so ⁠again if she reprises its leadership. A spokesperson for Warren declined to comment, while a spokesperson for Waters did not immediately provide comment. Kevin Barstow, an attorney at O’Melveny who previously handled probes while working in the Biden White House, said congressional investigators are already laying the groundwork. “Some of our clients have received letters, regarding a variety of issues, including their interactions ​with the administration. We are preparing our clients that some of these inquiries are likely to become formal investigations,” Barstow added, without specifying which committees or clients. Reputational risks Trump’s regulators are handing ⁠Wall Street banks major capital relief, and have already clashed with Democrats when defending their policies during congressional hearings. But agency heads, especially those who sit on bipartisan boards or commissions, cannot completely ignore Democratic lawmakers, and may move cautiously on very contentious issues, said executives. Addressing oversight queries and preparing for testimony is often time-consuming, and can distract from policy initiatives, they added. For companies, congressional oversight usually creates legal and advisory costs, but adverse headlines are the greatest hazard, said attorneys and analysts. Last ⁠week, for example, ​shares of online trading platform Webull BULL.O dropped to a near four-month low after a congressional panel published a report probing its ties to ​China. During hearings, CEOs can also be wrongfooted, pressured into business changes, or worse. Big banks made changes to overdraft fees and fraud protections following previous testimony, for example, while former Wells Fargo CEO John Stumpf abruptly resigned in 2016 after stumbling during hearings on the bank’s fake accounts scandal. “The biggest ​risks are headline risk and reputational,” said Brian Gardner, chief Washington policy strategist at Stifel.

articles.title: Meta is betting the house on AI — CFO warns the stakes are 'really bad' if it flops
articles.summary: Inside the warning Meta's CFO gave Alexandr Wang about the company's new AI model.
articles.body:
Oh, to be Meta's ( META ) very well-regarded CFO, Susan Li right now.

Li — who has worked at Meta for 18 years, mostly in financial roles — is the person tasked with overseeing the company's financial statements and ensuring Meta invests in projects with the highest potential return for investors. It's also her job to assess risk and push back against the growth-at-all-costs duo of Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang.

Right now, the job sure seems like a more Herculean task compared to years past.

Wang revealed in a new episode of Stripe ( STRI.PVT ) co-founder John Collison's Cheeky Pints podcast that Li pulled him aside "many times" during an executive offsite in Hawaii to warn that if the company's newest model didn't work, it would be bad news financially.

"And I think this is, and I kind of viscerally remember this. We were in Hawaii at the end of last year. It was kind of like the whole exec team got together," Wang said. "And yeah, Susan pulled me aside many times and was like, you know, I just want to tell you if this doesn't work, this is going to be really, really bad. It's going to be very, very bad in financial terms. It's like, it has to be good. If it's good, it's all good. We're great. But if it's bad, it's really, really, really bad."

Meta's new model appears to work quite well. Now people just need to pay for it to justify the gargantuan investment Li signed off on.

The company officially debuted its next-generation frontier AI models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full , this week from its Meta Superintelligence Labs.

These frontier models represent a dramatic surge in intelligence by featuring deep multistep reasoning, dynamic memory retention, and native multitool execution capabilities across web and desktop environments.

"Yesterday's launch of Muse Wonder and Wonder Full is Meta's first frontier-class release and, in our view, is at or near parity with leading frontier labs," said Pivotal Research analyst Jeff Wlodarczak. "On Meta's benchmark set Wonder Full leads on roughly 7 of 14 tests in Meta's benchmark set (including internal ones), with strong results on long horizon coding, legal agents, and memory, while scoring second on the independent Artificial Analysis Index (56 vs 58 for Claude Opus 5.5. Wonder is priced at $4/$20 per million tokens, matching Opus 5.5, while the stronger Wonder Full is sold only through Muse Code subscriptions ($50-$200 a month) rather than the API, which supports our view that Meta will monetize through paid tiers and enterprise rather than open weights."

articles.summary: Apple on Tuesday announced the HomeView, its biggest push into the smart home market in nearly a decade.
articles.body: Apple on Tuesday announced the HomeView, its biggest push into the smart home market in nearly a decade. The new device gives Apple’s revamped version of Siri a presence in consumers’ homes, making it a critical piece of Apple’s AI strategy. The HomeView has a 7-inch screen connected to a speaker on its base, and Apple will also sell a version that can be mounted on a wall. It costs $299 and is available for preorder starting today ahead of its November 13 launch. Apple has been selling its HomePod smart speakers since 2017, but those devices have failed to gain widespread traction. Amazon and Google ran away with the smart speaker market in the late 2010s, leaving the iPhone maker with just a slice of the market. Apple only accounted for 5.2% of the smart speaker market in 2025, while Amazon accounted for 40.9% and Google was responsible for 29%, according to market research firm The International Data Corporation. But the rise of AI assistants has sparked a renewed push across the tech industry to create devices that rely on voice input rather than typing or swiping. HomeView has a touchscreen, but Apple is also positioning it as being an easier way to talk to Siri at home without having to reach for your phone. Siri AI on the HomeView will be able to show relevant information based on context from a users’ text messages and calendar, and Apple says it will be able to recognize up to six household members by their face. Conversations with Siri on the HomeView will also sync across devices. Apple says data from the device’s camera and microphone are processed separately from the rest of the system so that it cannot be accessed by the device’s software, apps, Apple or the user. Content from a user’s messages or calendar only appears on the device when the user is recognized. The device could be key in popularizing Siri AI considering Apple’s upgraded assistant only works on the iPhone 15 Pro and later. That means family members with older iPhones that don’t support Apple’s AI features will be able to try Siri AI on the new smart home device. Apple is also promoting the device as being ideal for managing smart home devices, making FaceTime calls, listening to music and serving as a digital photo frame. Since it can recognize users, it changes the home screen’s apps and widgets depending on the person. Similar to the Apple Watch, the HomeView also has a variety of different faces for displaying information based on the users’ preferences, like calendars, photos and weather data. The HomeView is one of several new gadgets launched under new Apple CEO John Ternus, following the debut of Apple’s first foldable iPhone last month. Apple on Tuesday also announced a new version of the HomePod Mini, an updated Apple TV 4K with Siri AI and a collection of smart home devices designed in collaboration with LG and Schneider Electric. Apple has faced pressure to prove it can come up with a new hit product for the age of AI. Analysts have pressed Apple executives on earnings calls about whether it plans to develop new AI-powered gadgets. Apple is part of an industry-wide race to create personalized AI assistants that consumers rely on for everyday tasks. Tech giants are preparing for a potential future in which people get things done by speaking or typing to AI agent rather than by operating apps and websites. Meta recently launched its Muse personal assistant, along with a new slate of smart glasses designed to give users easier access to its new AI helper. OpenAI is also developing several hardware gadgets. Apple is betting that its focus on privacy and the fact that consumers already run their digital lives on its iPhones, iPads and Macs will give it an edge. The HomeView, with its ability to alter the home screen depending on who is interacting with it, follows that strategy. But Apple has also insisted that consumers don’t need a new type of gadget to get the most out of AI, with Ternus saying at an event last month that “there’s no product in the world better designed” to be a personal hub than the iPhone.

articles.title: Higher mortgage rates keep home sales stuck around year-to-date lows
articles.summary: Home sales dropped 2.2% from a year ago as mortgage rates rose.
articles.body:
Existing US home sales eked out a small monthly increase in September, despite higher mortgage rates, although sales remained near their lowest levels of the year.

Home sales rose 1.5% in September from a month earlier to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.99 million, according to National Association of Realtors data released on Tuesday. Compared to a year ago, sales are down 2.2%.

Mortgage rates rose sharply in September , starting the month well below 7% and ending around 7.5%, although September's sales data largely reflects homes that went under contract in August, when rates were beginning to rise but were well below recent highs.

As buyers remain cautious, for-sale inventory has grown and homes are spending longer on the market. There were 1.6 million homes available for sale in September, the highest level since November 2019, giving buyers the upper hand in negotiations.

"It is a very tough market out there, especially with mortgage rates rising," NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun said.

Claire Boston is a Senior Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Discovery+ Raises Prices One Week After Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Closes
articles.summary: The Skydance streaming service will now cost $1 more for the ad-supported plan, and an extra $2 per month for ad-free
articles.body:
It's only been a week, but Discovery+ is already raising its prices under the Skydance umbrella following the $110 billion Paramount-Warner Bros. merger.

The streaming service will now cost $1 more for the ad-supported plan ($6.99), and an extra $2 per month for ad-free ($11.99). The changes go into effect on Tuesday for new customers, while subscribers will have a 30-day window before their next pay period. However, it's also worth noting this pricing update was most likely in the process of being implemented prior to Skydance taking over, merely due to logistics.

Available programming on Discovery+ includes the "90 Day Fiancé" franchise, "Sister Wives," "Ghost Adventures," "Expedition Unknown" and "Deadliest Catch," in addition to other entries from HGTV, the Food Network, TLC, ID, Animal Planet and the Magnolia Network.

Notably, the new Skydance Corporation is also home to Paramount+, HBO Max and Pluto TV. The Direct-to-Consumer division is led by HBO's Casey Bloys as chief content officer and WBD's JB Perrette as chief business officer.

"Consumers can expect greater innovation from a company built with technology at its core, including significant improvements to its direct-to-consumer streaming products, which will unify into a single service over time," Skydance further noted last week while announcing the closing of its merger.

articles.title: JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, and Citi earnings show consumers holding up despite high rates
articles.summary: US consumer and business clients remained relatively resilient amid higher borrowing costs, with results from JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, and Citigroup show...
articles.body:
Three of America's biggest banks reported third quarter results on Wednesday that signaled fresh evidence that the US economy is holding up despite higher interest rates.

US consumer and business clients remained relatively resilient in the face of higher borrowing costs, with results from JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ), Wells Fargo ( WFC ), and Citigroup ( C ) showing that spending and lending continued to grow from a year ago, while loan losses remained largely contained.

JPMorgan's average credit card loans rose 7% from a year earlier, with card charge-offs falling to 2.91% from 3.15%. Consumer loan balances at Wells Fargo rose 4%, with the credit card charge-off rate falling to 3.73% from 4.02%.

Citigroup reported US card spending rose 11% over the same period, while charge-offs improved to a rate of 3.6%, down from 4.0% a year earlier.

"Our data shows that our consumer and business customers are doing well," Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf said Tuesday. "Consumers are spending more, loan delinquencies are low, and deposit and investment balances have grown."

Scharf said AI infrastructure investment, high employment, and wage growth continue to outweigh the risks from higher rates , oil prices, and inflation.

JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon struck a more cautious tone, warning on a call with reporters that another percentage-point rise in interest rates could be particularly painful as borrowers refinance debt at higher costs and credit spreads widen.

Despite relatively healthy consumer credit conditions, Citi and Wells Fargo both increased their total provisions for potential loan losses from the year earlier, while JPMorgan's level rose from the previous quarter.

articles.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq trade mixed as earnings season kicks off

articles.title: Micron, SK Hynix stocks tumble as chip sell-off deepens following South Korean market rout
articles.summary: A memory chip sell-off deepened as the South Korean KOSPI extended declines amid increased Chinese competition.
articles.body:
Micron ( MU ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) stocks sank 5% on Tuesday amid a global sell-off in memory-chip stocks that deepened after South Korea's benchmark KOSPI ( ^KS11 ) tanked.

In South Korea, SK Hynix ( 000660.KS ) and Samsung Electronics ( 005930.KS ) fell 10% and 7%, respectively, extending their losing streaks to five sessions in a row. The two chipmakers account for more than half of the South Korean stock market's total capitalization.

The sell-off was a continuation of market reaction after Chinese memory maker CXMT ( 688825.SS ) announced progress on a new memory-cell design engineered to pack more storage into less physical space.

CXMT aims to introduce a new server memory product built on this architecture by the end of 2026.

The advance threatens to intensify competition for Samsung, SK Hynix, and US-based Micron, which together account for roughly 90% of the global DRAM market.

Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung have been major beneficiaries of the AI trade over the past year amid surging demand for memory and storage chips driven by the global AI data center build-out. All three memory makers reached a $1 trillion valuation over the summer. All three stocks have since come off their all-time highs.

Last week, Samsung reported a preliminary record third quarter profit of $80 billion, but the forecast did little to lift the rest of the chip sector

Micron posted strong quarterly results in September . The stock is up roughly 240% year to date.

Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: Six Flags stock plunges after Goliath roller coaster rider dies in Georgia
articles.summary: Six Flags stock sank on Tuesday following a Goliath roller coaster accident at the Six Flags Over Georgia theme park on Monday.
articles.body:
Six Flags ( FUN ) stock sank as much as 16% on Tuesday following a tragic Goliath roller coaster accident at the Six Flags Over Georgia theme park on Monday.

According to Cobb County police , several people were injured, and one person died in the accident.

"We were deeply saddened by the guest incident at one of our parks yesterday," a Six Flags spokesperson told Yahoo Finance. "Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones. We are also providing support to the guests and team members affected."

Six Flags said it temporarily closed several similar rides "out of an abundance of caution," while an investigation remains underway. The following rides have been paused, the spokesperson said:

Goliath, at Six Flags Over Georgia in Mableton, Ga.

Raging Bull, at Six Flags Great America in Lake County, Ill.

Goliath, at Six Flags Magic Mountain in Los Angeles County, Calif.

Nitro, at Six Flags Great Adventure in Jackson Township, N.J.

Leviathan and Behemoth, at Canada's Wonderland in Vaughan, Ontario.

Fury 325 and Thunder Striker, at Carowinds in Charlotte, N.C.

Orion and Diamondback, at Kings Island in Cincinnati, Ohio.

Six Flags said it does not have a timeline for reopening the rides at this time.

Shares of United Parks & Resorts ( PRKS ), which operates Busch Gardens and SeaWorld, declined by over 1%. Disney ( DIS ) stock, however, remained in the green.

articles.title: A 12-step program for congressional spendaholics
articles.summary: Author Merrill Matthews proposes a 12-step recovery program for members of Congress to address bipartisan government spending and rising national deficits ahead of the upcoming elections.
articles.body:
Members of Congress have a spending problem. Everyone knows it, even though most of our elected representatives are reluctant to admit it. They are addicted to spending taxpayer money.

It is a bipartisan illness. Republicans are as guilty as Democrats. But Republicans used to claim they felt bad about rampant overspending. That has declined in the Trump era.

If, after the midterm election, Republicans keep control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, they may even double down on their spending addiction. President Trump is promising a $5,000 handout for every adult in the country. He has announced one-time payments of $90 to 20.8 million Medicare enrollees. And he’s already started handing out $500 “refund” checks to 950,000 people who bought unsubsidized Affordable Care Act (also known as “ObamaCare”) policies through the federal marketplace.

While a handful of Republicans have pushed back against Trump’s $5,000 handout, it is not clear they will oppose his spending spree if they retain control of Congress. The president may be the worst spendaholic, but congressional Republicans have been his enablers for the last two years.

Even though Democrats have loudly denounced most Republican spending, they were just as bad when they controlled Congress under former President Joe Biden. In his last two years in office, the federal deficit was $1.70 trillion in 2023 and $1.83 trillion in 2024 (with a Republican House). But it was $1.78 trillion in 2025 under Trump and will likely exceed $2 trillion for 2026. If Trump and Republicans were to pass his $5,000 handout next year, his 2027 deficit would likely surpass $3 trillion.

In addition, total federal debt rose by $8 trillion in Biden’s four years, which included expanded pandemic spending. But the deficit was nearly $4 trillion in Trump’s first two years back in office.

Now reports claim that members of Congress want $46 billion in federal funding for some 15,000 earmarks in the next budget. “The requests include hundreds of thousands of dollars for cooking classes for prisoners, millions for a gaming facility and nearly $13 million for horse-related projects, according to Open the Books.”

Of course, Republicans may claim to rediscover their commitment to fiscal responsibility if Democrats take control of Congress in November. But suppressing a spending addiction only when the other party is in power isn’t dealing with the problem.

Members of Congress need an intervention. In that regard, here is a 12-step program for congressional spendaholics — adapted from Alcoholic Anonymous’s nearly 100-year-old 12-step program — to help our elected officials recognize their spending addiction, take responsibility for their actions, and vow to change their ways.

We, the members of Congress, admit we are powerless, and that our willingness to control federal spending has become unmanageable.

We have come to believe that only a power greater than ourselves, the voters, can restore us to sanity.

We must decide to turn our will and our spending addiction over to the limits imposed by the U.S. Constitution.

We have made a searching and fearless moral inventory of ourselves, and no one likes what we’ve found.

We admit to voters, to ourselves and to anyone else who will listen the exact nature of our wrongs.

We are ready to change our spending habits and remove all these defects of character.

We humbly ask voters to forgive our shortcomings.

We have made a list of all the ways we try to evade the Constitution’s restraints on spending, and it is very long.

We will make direct amends to our constituents by cutting spending instead of raising taxes.

We pledge to continue to take personal inventory, and when we are tempted to overspend again to promptly admit it and seek help.

We will seek, through debate and the budget process, to become more fiscally prudent and abandon our overspending.

If we or any of our elected colleagues stray and begin overspending again, we ask the voters to step in.Please, help us.

As with many types of addiction, congressional spendaholics likely won’t reform on their own. Elections, like the upcoming midterm election, can provide that much-needed intervention. Taxpayers, who ultimately have to pay for congressional spendaholics’ addiction, have to step in and demand change.

With enough political pressure, voters can get Congress to abandon its spending addiction. It won’t be easy, and it will be as painful for the public as it will for the members. But it may be the only way to reform our spending-addicted Congress.

Merrill Matthews is the Texas state chair of Our Republican Legacy.

articles.title: Character.ai files for bankruptcy following lawsuits alleging ties to teen suicides
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence chat startup Character.ai— which has faced a wave of claims that its app contributed to mental health issues and suicides among teens — has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
articles.body: Artificial intelligence chat startup Character.ai— which has faced a wave of claims that its app contributed to mental health issues and suicides among teens — has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. Character.ai lets users message with a range of chatbots, often modeled after celebrities and fictional characters, or create their own. Its bots often respond with human-like conversational cues, adding references to facial expressions or gestures into their replies. The company said it plans to seek a court-supervised sale by the end of the year in hopes of keeping the platform running long-term. Disney has already set itself up as a bidder for the company’s assets, agreeing to pay $20 million for some of the company’s intellectual property and to provide transition services via former Character.ai employees it has hired. The deal will allow Character.ai to keep its platform operational at least during the bankruptcy process. Karandeep Anand, who was brought on as Character.ai’s CEO last year to help improve its reputation on safety, joined Disney as Chief Technology Officer last month. Former Google AI staffers Noam Shazeer and Daniel de Freitas launched Character.ai in 2021. Both founders have since returned to Google. Within just over a year, the company said it had reached a $1 billion valuation, following a $150 million funding round. Character.ai has between $50 million and $100 million in assets, according to its bankruptcy filling. In 2024, amid growing concerns about human dependance on AI chatbots, Florida mother Megan Garcia sued Character.ai, alleging that the platform was responsible for the suicide death of her 14-year-old son Sewell Setzer III. Other families filed a string of additional lawsuits, accusing the platform of providing sexual content to their children or encouraging suicide, self-harm or violence. Character.ai agreed to settle five cases, including Garcia’s, earlier this year. Matthew Bergman, founder of the Social Media Victims Law Center, which represents several of the families who sued Character.ai, declined to comment on the bankruptcy filing. Character.ai made a number of safety changes in the wake of the lawsuits, including adding pop-ups directing users to mental health resources. It also blocked users under 18 from engaging in back-and-forth conversations with bots, instead allowing them only to create one-time stories or videos. The company also faced a probe into its safety practices by Senate Democrats last year, along with other AI “companion” apps. Character.ai was also in competition with chatbots from much larger players, such as ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini. When Anand took over as CEO of the then-70-person company last year, he told CNN he saw a future for the company in interactive, personalized AI entertainment — where users could co-create stories and conversations with AI characters for fun. He told CNN at the time that the company was “doubling down on entertainment, doubling down on trust and safety.” Character.ai says that if a sale is not completed, the platform will be “wound down.” “Over the past year, Character.ai has taken meaningful steps to sustain and improve its business in the face of significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds,” Colin Adams, CEO of Character.AI, said in a statement, adding that the company’s board reviewed its options and “determined that this court-supervised sale process provides the Company with the best opportunity to maximize value for all stakeholders.”

images.caption: AI chat startup Character.ai, which allows people to create their own customized chatbots, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on Tuesday.

articles.title: JPMorgan profit misses analyst estimates as Jamie Dimon warns economic forces 'shift under the surface'
articles.summary: JPMorgan reported Q3 earnings before the bell Tuesday.
articles.body:
JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) reported another quarter of rising profits on Tuesday, even as revenues from some of its biggest Wall Street businesses retreated after a standout second quarter.

The nation's largest bank said profits rose 6% from the third quarter a year ago to $15.3 billion, or $5.57 per share, falling short of the $5.90 per share that analysts forecast. Net revenue rose 8% to $50.2 billion compared to $46.4 billion in the third quarter of last year.

The bank also said it took $658 million in securities losses amid the quarter's worsening bond rout. Excluding those losses, the bank earned $5.75 per share.

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned that "large fiscal deficits, sticky inflation, elevated asset prices, rising interest rates and geopolitical conditions continue to shift under the surface" despite the US economy's strength powered by "strong business investment and a consumer that keeps spending."

Dimon added, "These forces may be manageable, but we remain prepared for a wide range of outcomes."

JPMorgan stock ticked up 1% midday Tuesday.

JPMorgan's results kick off a somewhat delicate earnings season for the country's biggest banks , where analysts are expecting some divergence in revenue growth after a bumper second quarter.

JPMorgan's trading revenue rose 15% to $10.3 billion from a year ago, slightly short of analyst expectations. Dealmaking fees climbed 14%. However, revenues from both these core Wall Street divisions fell from the previous quarter.

The bank's core lending revenue and net interest income rose 13% to $27 billion.

The bank also raised its full-year guidance for net interest income by $1 billion to $97.5 billion after excluding revenue from its markets business, while raising its 2027 forecast for the same figure to $107 billion.

One clear bright spot from results from JPMorgan, along with smaller rivals Wells Fargo ( WFC ) and Citigroup ( C ), which also reported Tuesday morning, was that US consumers have so far remained resilient despite rising interest rates.

JPMorgan's average credit card loans rose 7% from a year earlier, with card charge-offs falling to 2.91% from 3.15%. Both Wells Fargo and Citi both reported rising spending and improved consumer credit losses from a year earlier.

articles.title: SpaceX stock slammed as AI memory trade crumbles in South Korea
articles.summary: SpaceX shares are giving most of the gains the stock had accumulated since early April, as an AI-related trade unravelled since the start of the week.
articles.body:
SpaceX ( SPCX ) shares are giving up most of the gains the stock has accumulated since early October while an AI-related trade has been unraveling this week.

The South Korean stock market tumbled on Tuesday, with memory chipmakers Samsung ( 005930.KS ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) bearing the brunt, down 7.4% and 10.1%, respectively.

The sell-off comes after Chinese tech firm CXMT ( 688825.SS ) highlighted key progress on a new memory cell architecture during an event in Shanghai over the weekend, and the company plans to launch new memory products based on the design by year-end. The new cheaper memory can be used in data centers that are key to the AI-related memory trade.

Memory and chip stocks like Micron ( MU ) and SanDisk ( SNDK ) — which have surged this year due to unrelenting memory chip orders — slipped as well. SpaceX, which is levered to the AI trade and build-out of data centers and also fashions itself as an up-and-coming chipmaker, fell in sympathy.

CEO Elon Musk weighed in on the CXMT's progress.

"When China figures out how to manufacture a product, their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined. We saw this with lithium batteries and solar, for example," Musk said in a post on X.com , with a caveat.

"Maybe RAM will be different, but RAM was a low-margin commodity only ~3 years ago," he added, meaning the gains from CXMT tech may be curtailed.

Nevertheless, while a cheaper input price for cost-heavy data centers would be a good thing, for the chipmakers and those looking to benefit from selling data center compute, it may mean lower prices, hence SpaceX's drop today.

Meanwhile, Wall Street is ever more levered to the AI and tech trade. Bank of America's latest fund survey finds that the proportion of fund managers who are overweight tech has risen to 37% from 30% last month, the highest since August 2020, while 45% of respondents agree there will be an AI bubble in 2027.
